newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stock market racks up impressive year.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stock market racks up impressive year.

text.p: The numbers are still rolling in but the Toronto Stock Exchange, Canada's largest, has racked up impressive gains in volume and value this year among other statistics, the exchange said on Friday.
As of December 19, trading value jumped 43.1 percent to C$297.16 billion from a total of C$207.67 billion last year, according to preliminary information from TSE's information services department.
During the same time, total trading in Toronto's stock market jumped 39.5 percent to 21.99 billion shares from 15.76 billion shares in 1995, the TSE said.

Toronto's stock market -- the 10th most active equities market world-wide measured by value -- also had 173 new issues listed as of December 19, the highest number since 190 in 1987. Toronto also had 168 new companies listed, another high since 180 in 1987.
The number of initial public offerings reached 79, the most since 89 in 1993.
Some of Toronto's stocks posted spectacular gains and losses during the year.
Leading the pack in price increases was Fairfax Financial Holdings Ltd, which soared by 177 dollars to close at 275 on December 18, up from a year low of 98.
On Friday the investment management and insurance firm added another 6.50 to reach 287, a little underneath its year high of 310.
International telephone service provider Teleglobe Inc preferred shares, series 2, jumped by 42.25 to 85.00 by December 18.
Arequipa Resources, bought out by giant Barrick Gold Corp in late summer for C$1 billion, surged from the opening price of 2.35 at the beginning of 1996 to a final price of 29.95.

Investors saw some shares suffer large losses as well. Among the year's biggest losers was Legacy Storage Systems International Inc. It opened at more than 29.00 but lost nearly all its value to close at 2.86 as of December 18.
The company said it would divest itself of its systems business during a restructuring to focus on the tape date storage business after posting serious losses this year.
Technology firm Gandalf Technologies lost 17.70 to end at 5.30 after a year of difficulties with products.
